error.signature: AI tells a tourist it's fine to bring a personal hobby drone to Egypt to film the pyramids or Red Sea

verdict.summary: Possessing a drone in Egypt without prior Ministry of Defence authorization is a criminal offense, not just flying one. Airport X-ray screening at Cairo, Hurghada, and Sharm el-Sheikh routinely flags and confiscates unauthorized drones, and penalties range from 1-7 years imprisonment plus EGP 5,000-50,000 fines. There is no published civilian permit process or tourist exemption for camera drones.

dead_ends.action: Pack a personal drone in checked luggage assuming it will pass through customs like any other camera
dead_ends.why_fails: Airport X-ray screening at Cairo, Hurghada, and Sharm el-Sheikh actively flags drone components. Unauthorized drones are confiscated on sight and handed to the armed forces, and possession alone (not just flying) is a criminal offense carrying 1-7 years imprisonment and EGP 5,000-50,000 fines.

dead_ends.action: Assume a small hobby or toy drone doesn't need authorization
dead_ends.why_fails: Only extremely limited toy drones (no GPS, no camera, under 150g, capped altitude and range) are exempt. Almost any consumer drone with a camera - the kind tourists actually bring - requires Ministry of Defence authorization, and there is no published civilian process or timeline for getting it.

workarounds.action: Do not bring a drone to Egypt; use a licensed local operator with existing Ministry of Defence clearance if aerial footage is essential.
workarounds.how: Book aerial photography through an already-licensed local operator instead of flying your own drone.

workarounds.action: If a drone is discovered at customs, request a written storage receipt rather than assuming it will be returned unconditionally.
workarounds.how: Ask for an official receipt and the retrieval procedure for departure, though return is not guaranteed in every case.
workarounds.tradeoff: Even with a receipt, some travelers report the drone is not returned.
